name: RoboBench
description: RoboBench is a comprehensive benchmark that systematically evaluates multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains for robotic manipulation. It defines five dimensions—instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis—spanning 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs. The benchmark covers diverse embodiments, attribute-rich objects, multi-view scenes, and memory-driven navigation, drawing from large-scale real robotic data and in-house collection. It introduces an MLLM-as-world-simulator evaluation framework for planning that assesses embodied feasibility by simulating whether predicted plans can achieve critical object-state changes under physical and visual constraints.
creator: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang
publisher: Peking University, Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence, Fudan University, University of Science and Technology Beijing, Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics
citeAs: Luo, Y., Fan, C.-K., Dong, M., Shi, J., Zhao, M., Zhang, B.-W., et al. (2025). RoboBench: A Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models as Embodied Brain. arXiv:2510.17801.
rai:dataCollection: Datasets are built from open-source and in-house robotic data, enriched with MLLM- and human-provided annotations. Instruction comprehension data uses explicit instructions from daily-life scenarios rewritten into implicit forms using LLMs. Perception reasoning data is constructed across robotic-centric, object-centric, scene-centric, and task-centric aspects using real robot data, curated static attributes, GPT-generated functional properties, Gemini-segmented video steps, and human-labeled bounding boxes. Generalized planning data is built from high-quality robotic videos with Gemini-generated structured annotations refined by human annotators. Affordance prediction data samples representative frames from the planning pool annotated with three types of affordance. Failure analysis data collects execution-level failures from RoboMIND labeled by experts, while planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Web Scraping
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Large-scale real-world robotic datasets including RH20T (Fang et al., 2023), Open X-Embodiment (Collaboration et al., 2023), RDT-FT, ARIO, DSL, OXE, EgoCOT, RoboMIND (Wu et al., 2024), AGIBot World (Bu et al., 2025), and other sources including ScanNet, ScanNetPP, ARKitScenes, as well as in-house collected robotic video data.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Explicit task instructions are rewritten into implicit (demand-based) forms using LLMs. Natural language step descriptions from videos are mapped to predefined function sequences. Function arguments are instantiated with specific object references. Planning-level failure data is synthesized by perturbing correct instructions (wrong object, missing step, wrong order).
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A two-stage quality control process is applied: (1) data filtering during construction using general criteria (image quality, task validity) and task-specific filters (e.g., excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks); (2) post-construction validation by 20 professionally trained annotators checking linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness. A majority-vote strategy is applied: items all models solve correctly are removed, and items all models fail are manually reviewed and corrected. All data are standardized into multiple-choice QA or planning/point-prediction formats.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations are created through a combination of automated and human methods. Gemini generates structured annotations for planning tasks including task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata (objects, actions, scenes, embodiments). Human annotators refine these annotations. For perception tasks, human annotators label bounding boxes linking instructions to target objects, and manually annotate relative positions and keypoint changes. Execution-level failure data is labeled by expert annotators. For affordance prediction, representative frames are annotated with static (contact points), dynamic (motion trajectories), and mobile (base positions) affordances. For evaluation, expert annotators assign holistic scores (0-20) to planning outputs referencing ground-truth planning lists and considering skill selection, object identification, and plan executability.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A majority-vote strategy is used: items that all models solve correctly are removed as too easy, while items all models fail undergo manual review and correction. For planning evaluation validity, a human study on 438 sampled long-horizon tasks compared the MLLM-as-world-simulator method against an LLM-based pairwise trajectory scoring baseline using Pearson correlation with human judgments. The proposed method achieved higher correlation (r=0.83) compared to the baseline (r=0.73).
rai:annotatorDemographics: 20 professionally trained annotators conducted comprehensive quality inspections.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini (Comanici et al., 2025) for structured annotation generation (task summaries, step-wise instructions, timestamps, metadata); GPT for generating functional object properties and distractors; Gemini for video segmentation into steps for temporal grounding; detection models for annotation assistance.
rai:dataSocialImpact: RoboBench provides a comprehensive scaffold to quantify high-level cognition of MLLMs as embodied brains, clarify the role of the embodied brain in robotic systems, and guide the development of next-generation MLLMs toward more robust robotic intelligence. It establishes a leaderboard and offers actionable insights for advancing embodied AI in manipulation tasks.
rai:dataBiases: Planning data primarily focuses on concrete action execution without explicitly distinguishing between left-right arm assignments or positional movements, which may bias cross-embodiment planning evaluation. Planning-level failure data is synthesized rather than collected from real-world failures due to lack of real-world planning failure data, which may not fully represent the distribution of real failures.
rai:dataLimitations: Planning-level failure data is synthesized by perturbing correct instructions rather than collected from real-world planning failures, due to lack of such data. The benchmark focuses on manipulation tasks and may not generalize to other embodied AI domains. Multi-view inputs yield only modest planning gains and do not close the gap to human performance.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation and benchmarking of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains for robotic manipulation. Specifically used for testing across five dimensions: instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis. The benchmark supports leaderboard comparison of state-of-the-art MLLMs and provides insights for developing next-generation embodied AI systems.
